chunks: Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Fudayl, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

He said to me: O Abu Ubaydah! Beware of the quarrelers and the liars about us, for they have left what they were ordered to know and have strived for the knowledge of Heaven. O Abu Ubaydah! Accustom people according to their dispositions and distance yourself from them according to their deeds. We do not consider a man among us to be wise until he recognizes the tone of speech.
And most certainly you will recognize them by the tone of (their) speech.

key_terms.أَصْحَاب الْخِصْمَات: Quarrelers or those prone to disputes
key_terms.خَالِقُوا النَّاس: Accustom or mold people (literally: make them with/create them with)
key_terms.زَايِلُوهُمْ: Distance yourself from them or separate from them
key_terms.عِلْم السَّمَاء: Knowledge of Heaven, often referring to esoteric or elevated knowledge sought by some groups
key_terms.لَحْن الْقَوْل: Tone or accent of speech, used here to indicate a distinctive mark of recognition

ai.seo_question: What does 'lahn al-qawl' mean in Shia hadith and how does it relate to recognizing the Imams?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) warns against the 'Kadhibun' (liars) who fabricate traditions to gain authority, contrasting their superficial debate with the Imams' profound wisdom. He emphasizes that true discernment lies in recognizing the 'lahn al-qawl' (distinctive tone/accent of speech), a concept linking linguistic precision to spiritual authenticity, while advising social adaptability ('khalluq al-nas bi-akhlaqihim') to maintain harmony. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on verifying narrators not just by chain, but by their alignment with the Imams' intellectual and spiritual character.
